summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react-native-web preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package's preinstall script (invoked via `node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun `bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`), extracts it, chmods it executable, and then runs the fetched Bun binary against `math_init.js`, a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle shipped in the tarball. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style identifier mangling, per-function string dictionaries, rotated string arrays), so the code that ultimately runs at install is not human-readable. The declared package entry (`jest-preset.js`, the advertised Jest preset) unconditionally throws `Use @ornikar/jest-config-react-native/web instead`, delivering no Jest configuration. The only functional install-time effect is the alternate-runtime dropper. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: a second JavaScript runtime is pulled in at install time solely to execute an obfuscated sibling module, bypassing Node-based analysis, on a package whose stated purpose has no need for Bun.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
